distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.heading: Theorem AP — sharp-bulk packing in a convex annulus
distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.source_statement_excerpt: Let `D>=1`. Let `F subset K` be compact convex planar sets with \[ \operatorname{diam}K\le D. \] Let `S subset K\setminus F` be finite and unit-separated. Then \[ \boxed{ |S| \le \frac2{\sqrt3} \bigl(\operatorname{area}K-\operatorname{area}F\bigr) +O(D^{3/2}), } \tag{AP.2} \] where the implied constant is universal. In particular, for any sequence with `D->infinity`, \[ \boxed{ |S| \le \frac2{\sqrt3} \operatorname{area}(K\setminus F) +o(D^2). } \tag{AP.3} \] No contact, KKT, triangle-free, or global-optimality hypothesis is used in AP.

distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.heading: Theorem MEX — no unbounded post-ZF perfect-matching survivor sequence
distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.source_statement_excerpt: Assume the audited/report-level post-ZF hypotheses used by MB and FSDB. There is no unbounded sequence of lexicographically normalized triangle-free global minimizers for which the **full actual diameter graph** is a perfect matching. Equivalently, along every sufficiently large post-ZF survivor sequence, the full actual diameter graph has at least one vertex of diameter degree at least two.

distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.heading: 5. Exact remaining lemma
distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.source_statement_excerpt: The shortest continuation is no longer “exclude a perfect matching.” A stronger branch theorem must turn the **amount** of diameter branching into source-capacity loss. One sufficient formulation is: > **Branched annular capacity theorem.** For every sufficiently large post-ZF survivor, use > \[ > r_H:=2h-q=x_B+Q+2s_Z\ge1 > \] > together with the full-source FS/PW geometry and the difference-body constraints to prove either > \[ > n-1\le\frac\pi{2\sqrt3}D^2 > \] > or construct an `n`-point unit-separated competitor of diameter `<D`. A more concrete near-matching subtarget is to prove a positive **linear** lower bound `r_H>=cD`; DB.1 would then force `h/D` above its minimum by a fixed amount, and FSDB's force-hull area constant would improve accordingly. MEX alone gives only `r_H>=1`, so such a linear upgrade is not claimed here. ---

distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.heading: 8. Failed routes and no-go results
distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.source_statement_excerpt: 1. A direct Oler inequality on `K` cannot subtract the empty force-hull area. AP succeeds only by localizing Oler to mesoscopic cells wholly outside `F` and paying separately for cells meeting either boundary. 2. A fixed-size cell decomposition would lose `Theta(D^2)` through Oler's per-cell boundary term. The cell side must satisfy `L->infinity`. 3. A macroscopic cell size `L=Theta(D)` would make the boundary-cell loss quadratic. The scale must also satisfy `L=o(D)`. The choice `L=sqrt(D)` balances the two errors. 4. MEX does not imply near-matching supports are impossible. A diameter graph with `2h-q=1` survives this proof in principle. ---

distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.source_statement_excerpt: Let `S subset R/pi Z` be a nonempty closed projective direction set of measure `s`. distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.source_statement_excerpt: Take `S=S(F_infty)` and `R=1/2`. Therefore \[ \operatorname{area}(F_\infty)\ge\frac{y+\sin y}{4}. \] Area is continuous under planar Hausdorff convergence. This proves ADA.2. ---

distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.source_statement_excerpt: Let `P subset K` be planar compact convex sets such that 1. `P` is a convex polygon; 2. every vertex of `P` is an extreme point of `K`; 3. `diam(K)=1`; 4. with \[ r:=\operatorname{diam}(P), \] one has \[ \frac{12}{25}=0.48\le r\le\frac12. \] Then \[ \boxed{ \operatorname{area}(P) < \frac\pi4r^2- rac1{2500}. } \tag{BVP.1} \] Thus a nested attachment polygon in this diameter range loses at least \[ \boxed{0.0004} \] of normalized area from the ordinary isodiametric disk bound. distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.heading: Lemma CP1 — deepest opposite cap stacks form a central phase block
distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.source_statement_excerpt: Let `Q` be one coherent residual train phase.  Every non-chain train in `Q` has both terminals on one of the two boundary arcs `L,U` from `z` to `a`.  Trains in `Q` are pairwise noncrossing. On one side, order the `Q`-trains by decreasing boundary-cap interval.  The cap intervals are nested.  A train omitted after a deepest prefix lies in the boundaryward cap of the last retained train. In the global order of the pairwise noncrossing phase family `Q`, the two side stacks therefore occur as `(shallow L ... deep L) | (deep U ... shallow U)` up to reversing the whole order.  Consequently the union of a deepest prefix from the L stack and a deepest prefix from the U stack is a **central contiguous block** of `Q`. Any omitted `Q`-train lies outside that block and does not separate any two vertices inside the central strip bounded by the retained extremal `Q`-trains.

distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.source_statement_excerpt: Every train track contains at most one positive chain edge. distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.heading: Lemma 1 — one distinct hull transition per chain terminal
distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.source_statement_excerpt: On each hull arc `L` and `U`, every terminal of `tau_j`, `1<=j<=D`, lies in a distinct indentation chain between consecutive convex-hull vertices. Hence there are exactly `2D` pairwise distinct distinguished hull indentation chains, one for each side-terminal incidence of the `D` chain trains.

distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.heading: Lemma 2 — at most two one-edge distinguished transitions
Theorem — chain-terminal hull-transition budget
distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.source_statement_excerpt: The number of two-edge distinguished transitions satisfies the exact finite bound `m_2 >= 4D+q-2T-4`. Using C96, `q>=2D+2`, this gives `m_2 >= 2(3D-T)-2`. In particular, for every asymptotic survivor with `T/D <= 3-epsilon`, there are at least `(2epsilon-o(1))D` two-edge hull indentation chains containing exactly one `P` terminal edge. Moreover, the non-`P` edge in each such two-edge chain is the terminal edge of a secondary train. Since one train has only two boundary terminals, at least `m_2/2 >= 2D+q/2-T-2` distinct secondary trains occur in this way. With C96, `# boundary-neighbor secondary trains >= 3D-T-1`.

scope_or_obligation_anchor.heading: 2. Scope and the whole-circuit exception
scope_or_obligation_anchor.source_scope_excerpt: If `S` omits at least one unloaded component, then `W(S)` omits all vertices of that component and is automatically proper. Thus AS.1 applies to every nonempty proper subfamily of unloaded components. If `S` is the full component family but some loaded vertex is unused by all attachments, then `W(S)` is still proper and AS.1 also applies. The unique exceptional case is \[ S=\{1,\ldots,c_I\}, \qquad A(S)=B_+. \tag{2.1} \] Then `W(S)=V(G_M)` and one must use the full circuit equality (1.1) instead of the proper-subset bound. Equation (1.4) becomes \[ 2(v-q)+c_I+s_C+e_{BB}+h=2v-2, \] so \[ \boxed{ s_C+e_{BB}+h=2q-c_I-2.} \tag{2.2} \] This is exactly one unit above the formal proper-subset right side `2q-c_I-3`, as required for a rigidity circuit. Thus AS.1 has the correct whole-circuit exception and does not silently apply proper-subset sparsity to the full graph. ---

distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.source_statement_excerpt: For every diameter endpoint `b`, `d_D(b) <= ceil(W_D/delta_D)`. distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.heading: Lemma F2 — global diameter-fan budget
distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.source_statement_excerpt: Let `F` be any forest contained in the complete diameter graph. If `m=|E(F)|` and `c` is the number of nontrivial connected components, then `(m-c) delta_D <= 2*pi`. Proof. If `d_F(b)` is the degree in `F`, then `(d_F(b)-1)delta_D <= alpha_b` at every nonisolated vertex. Sum over the nonisolated vertices. A forest with `m` edges and `c` nontrivial components has `v=m+c` incident vertices, so `sum_b(d_F(b)-1)=2m-v=m-c`. The sum of the corresponding exterior angles is at most `2*pi`. This proves the claim.

distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.heading: Theorem ID — universal cyclic interior descent
distinct_mathematical_content_anchors.source_statement_excerpt: Let `A` be a sufficiently large cyclic primitive triangle-free global minimizer of cardinality `n` and diameter \[ D=D(n). \] Let \[ Z:=A\setminus V(F), \qquad |Z|=n-q. \] Then \[ \boxed{ \operatorname{dist}(z,\partial F)>\frac{\sqrt3}{2} \qquad(z\in Z).} \tag{ID.1} \] Consequently \[ \boxed{ \operatorname{diam}Z<D-\sqrt3,} \tag{ID.2} \] and therefore the global optimum values satisfy \[ \boxed{ D(n-q)<D(n)-\sqrt3.} \tag{ID.3} \] This holds in all three cyclic diameter-topology phases. Because RP gives \[ q=\pi D-\frac\pi{24D}+O(D^{-2}), \tag{ID.4} \] ID is an exact one-step descent on the asymptotically natural shell scale: deleting approximately `pi D` source points decreases achievable diameter by strictly more than `sqrt(3)`. ---

scope_or_obligation_anchor.source_scope_excerpt: ```text LEVEL I STATUS: STILL OPEN. UFB: F=conv(A) in every cyclic phase. C-I/CY: the only actual unit contacts are the q unit hull-cycle edges. Therefore every interior point z has |z-p|>1 for every hull vertex p. Let r=dist(z,partial F). If nearest point is a hull vertex, r>1. If it lies inside a unit side, the nearer side endpoint is tangentially <=1/2 away, so 1<|z-p|^2<=r^2+1/4, therefore r>sqrt(3)/2. For the finite interior set Z, r_*=min depth>sqrt(3)/2. Since F_-r_* + r_* B subset F, every width drops by at least 2r_*: diam(Z)<=diam(F_-r_*)<=D-2r_*<D-sqrt3. Thus D(n-q)<=diam(Z)<D(n)-sqrt3. Together with RP q=pi D-pi/(24D)+O(D^-2), this is an exact one-step descent at the first-derivative scale of D(n)~sqrt(n/Delta). Next: second-order control of the global optimum sequence D(n). ```
